slides.title: Dispatch Copilot: launch, package and price

paragraphs.text: Dispatch Copilot: launch, package and price
Discussion document for the CEO and executive team, January 2027 planning
Brightwork
CEO and executive team
Fictional company; figures from the synthetic briefing pack
Executive summary
Launch Copilot in Q2 2027 in a Pro plan at $12 more per seat: about $2.5M of ARR, not $8M, just enough for 105% NRR, at the cost of a two-quarter mobile delay
Copilot works for volunteers, but paying buyers point to about $2.1M of add-on ARR, not $8M
–	Only 14% of beta accounts bought at $149, against 46% in the survey
–	After costs, the add-on would earn about $0.6M of gross profit a year
AI is a real but smaller threat than claimed; mobile reliability drives far more churn
–	Copilot wins back at most a third of the Routewise deals the sales memo claims
–	27% of churned accounts left over mobile reliability, against 6% over AI features
A Pro plan at $12 more per seat is the better package, with a usage allowance to hold margin
–	Pro earns about $2.5M of ARR and $0.8M of gross profit; the add-on $2.1M and $0.6M
–	Including 667 requests per seat keeps margin above the 75% floor
Launch on schedule: Pro can just close the NRR gap, and waiting costs more unless the rewrite works fast
–	Pro adds 4.3 percentage points of NRR against 4 needed; it needs 31% uptake
–	Waiting wins only if the rewrite would stop over half of mobile churn at once

The estimate is generous to the add-on
▪	Buyers convert at the beta's 14%, although beta accounts volunteered and are larger and more active than the base
▪	Buyers keep their test usage; the heaviest tenth of beta accounts average 14,500 requests a month
▪	Inference stays at the contract price of $0.009 a request, fixed through December 2027
▪	Uptake is counted at its full-year level; first-year revenue is lower while buyers sign up
A price per account draws the heaviest users: inference would absorb 41% of the add-on's revenue
1  Estimate by the team from the briefing pack; live formulas on the Calculations sheet of the source workbook

The $2.5M holds only if the 2023 precedent carries over
▪	The 2023 tier had no AI; nothing in the pack ties its 33% uptake to demand for Copilot
▪	At the paywall's 14% Pro adds only $1.1M; at the survey's 46% it adds $3.5M
▪	Upgraders average 6.2 seats; beta buyers were larger, which would raise the figure
▪	No account moves down from Core, and Core stays at $79 per seat
1  Estimate by the team from the briefing pack; the live formula is on the Calculations sheet of the source workbook
